title: Quiz: Build your own farm helper

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Hannah is choosing files for the Ridgeback staff helper. Which should she load?

answers.text: The current staff handbook, dated March 2026
answers.feedback: Yes. It's current, dated and answers the questions new staff ask most.

answers.text: The equipment and maintenance list Jack updated last month
answers.feedback: Yes. Staff ask about machinery every day, and this list says what to check and what to do when something breaks.

answers.text: The staff contact list with home addresses and next of kin
answers.feedback: No. Anyone using the helper could ask for those details. The handbook already points to the phone numbers on the office whiteboard.

answers.text: Last year's handbook, for the extra detail on the shed
answers.feedback: No. An old version mixes out-of-date rules with current ones. Copy anything still useful into the current handbook instead.

answers.text: This week's jobs list, swapped for the new one every Sunday
answers.feedback: Yes. It's useful as long as someone replaces it each week and re-runs the tests.

questions.feedback: Load current, dated documents staff need day to day. Keep out old versions and anything with staff personal details.

questions.question: Priya asks the helper how many days milk is withheld after a mastitis treatment. It replies "usually four days". None of the farm documents gives a number. What's the best fix?

answers.text: Leave it alone, because four days is a common withholding period
answers.feedback: No. Withholding periods depend on the product and dose. A guess here could put treated milk in the vat.

answers.text: Tell Priya to ask the helper again with a clearer question
answers.feedback: Rewording won't help. The documents don't contain the answer, so the helper has to say so.

answers.text: Upload a general dairy guide so it has a number to quote
answers.feedback: A general guide still won't match the product used on this cow. The treatment book holds the real date for each cow.

answers.text: Add a line to say when it's not in the documents and who to ask
answers.feedback: Right. The helper filled a gap with a guess. This line, plus a re-test, makes it point Priya to the treatment book and to Jack or Hannah.

questions.feedback: When the answer isn't in your documents, the helper should say so and send people to the right person. A confident guess on animal health is the worst outcome.

questions.question: The handbook says visitors sign in at the dairy office. This week's jobs list says the implement shed. Which instruction line should the helper follow?

answers.text: If documents disagree, go with the most recently dated one
answers.feedback: Tempting, but the newest file isn't always the right one. The jobs list might simply be wrong, and staff never see the clash.

answers.text: If documents disagree, show both answers and don't pick one
answers.feedback: Right. Staff see both places and know to check, and the owner finds out the documents need fixing.

answers.text: If documents disagree, treat the handbook as the official one
answers.feedback: This hides the clash. If the change in the jobs list was deliberate, staff end up at the wrong shed.

answers.text: If documents disagree, leave that topic out of the answer
answers.feedback: Staff get no answer and no warning, so the clash stays hidden.

questions.feedback: When two documents disagree, the helper shouldn't settle it. It should show both so a person can decide and fix the documents.

questions.question: The helper answers a question about the side-by-side and names the equipment list as its source. What counts as checking that answer?

answers.text: Seeing that a real document name is given as the source
answers.feedback: A helper can name the right file and still add something the file doesn't say.

answers.text: Asking the helper whether it's sure about the answer it gave
answers.feedback: It will usually say yes. Its confidence tells you nothing about the document.

answers.text: Opening the equipment list and finding the matching words
answers.feedback: Right. A pass means the section actually says what the answer says.

answers.text: Deciding whether the answer sounds sensible for a farm
answers.feedback: Plenty of wrong answers sound sensible. Only the document tells you what Ridgeback's rule is.

questions.feedback: A named source is only useful if you open it. Check that the words in the document match the answer.

questions.question: Hannah builds a chat agent in Amazon Quick and tests it in the preview. She then closes the browser to deal with a calving without selecting Launch chat agent. What happens?

answers.text: Quick saves it as a draft she can share in the morning
answers.feedback: No. Quick's guide says the agent isn't saved until you launch it.

answers.text: The preview is deleted and the agent isn't saved
answers.feedback: Right. Leaving without launching discards the preview. Her space and documents are still there.

answers.text: The agent goes live but only for Hannah's own account
answers.feedback: That's what happens after launching. A launched agent is private until shared, but this one was never launched.

answers.text: The agent is shared with staff using the last preview
answers.feedback: No. Nothing is shared until an agent is launched and then shared.

questions.feedback: In Amazon Quick, test in the preview, then select Launch chat agent. Leaving the setup page without launching deletes the preview.

questions.question: Jack says the "answer only from the documents" line is pointless once the space is linked to the agent. Why keep it?

answers.text: It makes the agent answer faster on a phone
answers.feedback: The line is about where answers come from. It has nothing to do with speed.

answers.text: Linking the space only works when that line is in the instructions
answers.feedback: Linking works without it. The line changes how the agent answers once it's linked.

answers.text: A linked agent can still add the model's general knowledge
answers.feedback: Right. Quick's guide says a linked agent answers from the language model's knowledge plus the linked space, so the line keeps it to your documents.

answers.text: Without it, the agent can read other farms' spaces
answers.feedback: No. The agent only uses spaces you link or have access to. The risk is general knowledge, not other farms.

questions.feedback: Loading documents limits where a helper looks, not what it adds. The instruction line and your tests keep it to your documents.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: When should Ridgeback re-run its three helper tests?

answers.text: After Jack swaps in the new weekly jobs list
answers.feedback: Yes. A new jobs list can bring a new disagreement with the handbook.

answers.text: After an instruction line is changed or added
answers.feedback: Yes. A changed line can fix one answer and break another.

answers.text: After Hannah updates a rule in the handbook
answers.feedback: Yes. Any document change can change the answers.

answers.text: Only when a staff member reports a wrong answer
answers.feedback: By then someone has already acted on it. Re-test when something changes, before staff find the problem.

answers.text: Only once, on the day the helper is first shared
answers.feedback: One test day isn't enough. The documents keep changing after that, so the answers can too.

questions.feedback: Re-test whenever a document, an instruction or the tool changes. Waiting for a complaint means staff find the problem first.

questions.question: The conflict test shows the handbook and jobs list disagree on visitor sign-in. Hannah decides it stays at the dairy office. What should happen next?

answers.text: Add an instruction line telling the helper to prefer the handbook
answers.feedback: That hides the problem. The jobs list is still wrong, and staff reading it on the whiteboard will still go to the shed.

answers.text: Remove the jobs list from the helper for good
answers.feedback: Staff lose the weekly jobs, and the wrong note is still on the whiteboard.

answers.text: Jack corrects the jobs list, then they re-run the test
answers.feedback: Right. Fix the document at its source, then re-test and note the result in the record.

answers.text: Tell staff not to ask the helper about visitors
answers.feedback: The documents still disagree, and staff stop trusting the helper.

questions.feedback: When documents disagree, fix the documents first. The owner decides, corrects the file, and the test is run again.
